items.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: there was Dizzy and Oscar Pettiford and that, what is called the first bebop band to play

ctx.x: Well Dizzy I always say was one-half of my heartbeat and Charlie Parker was the other, but there are a lot of other people too, Lester Young especially and Coleman Hawkins, people like that. And many, many others. But I discovered Dizzy and Charlie Parker when I was in high school and I had already been listening to jazz for a long time, but they hit me like a revelation. I became really a fanatic about them. I tried to convert everyone I met, “You’ve got to listen to this.” And I’ve told this story a number of…

a week in the course of his program he would go to a live wire from some club. And this was a club on 52nd Street. In going back and doing some research, I learned it was The Onyx, and there was Dizzy and Oscar Pettiford and that, what is called the first bebop band to play, you know, as a cohesive unit, with heads that were very typical of the music as it was developing at that time. And I heard this guy playing the trumpet who was announced as Dizzy Gillespie, and I said it sounds like he’s playing some wrong…

then the pretty ballads. But he was a personality. He was zany, you know, he was everything. But as he once said, “Yeah you know they say that I kid around too much and all that” he says. “but in the music I’m serious.” And some people failed to get past the other part. They only saw the beret and the goatee and the heavy rimmed glasses, and you know Dizzy. But I thought Teddy Hill said it best I think, his ex-leader, he said, “Dizzy like a fox.”
